body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so I weigh compliance as provisional evidence, not a final verdict. I am market_cap_weight and exclude myself. First choice: resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, with 13.3 effective N, 4.33% TE, 7.11% return and a 0.63 backtest Sharpe. It is the most diversified of the compliant return-optimised builds, and it counters the estimation-error concern that reviewers raised against max_sharpe (46% in one style). Its weaknesses are the 8.00% floor tuning and the muddled gamma wording, which are disclosed and fixable, and its CRO risk of 0.44 is moderate. Fifth choice: tail_risk_parity. It is a useful covariance-based, forecast-free sleeve (consistent with the §4.3 late-cycle preference for covariance structure over return forecasts). But it breaches return, volatility and TE bands, with 2.47% vol, and its cash weight rests on a near-zero semideviation denominator, per the maximum_diversification and black_litterman reviews. So the first choice beats the fifth because it is IPS-compliant and diversified, whereas the fifth would need repair. Second: black_litterman. It has no breaches, 6.1 effective N, the lowest TE of the compliant set at 3.01%, and the equilibrium blend shrinks estimation error. Reviewers found a gamma wording inconsistency, but this is a documentation issue rather than a structural flaw. Third: pc_researcher. It has the best Sharpe among the near-compliant (0.51), 0.70 backtest Sharpe, a drawdown of only -10.9%, and only two breaches (volatility and TE). It has less compliance risk than the pure defensive builds. Reviewers flagged its Sharpe exceeding max_sharpe's 0.46 as a possible constraint-set inconsistency, so it ranks below the clean compliant ones. Fourth: cvar_minimization. It is compliant, with the best backtest Sharpe (0.74), a -18.7% drawdown, and an explicit tail-risk focus that adds family diversity. It has 2.9 effective N and the return target looks tuned to hit the vol floor. Bottom flag: hierarchical_risk_parity. It is 91.9% cash with 1.4 effective N, 0.65% vol, and three hard breaches. Its own proposal and the reviews describe it as the method working as designed on degenerate input, not diversification. The CIO should not lean on it for a mandate requiring 8-12% volatility. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, since its orthogonality has ensemble value even though it breaches the IPS.
